title: Transactional Admin Playground with Undo Tokens and Staged Approvals
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a transactional 'Admin Playground' that allows engineers and first-line support to preview and safely execute multi-step runbook actions against staging or prod-like environments. Each change is encapsulated in a transaction that can be previewed, dry-run, and reversed using an immutable 'undo token'. The playground will integrate with existing runbook-as-task infra, require staged approval gates for risky operations, and emit structured telemetry for later regression analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Users can create a playground transaction bundling 1..n runbook steps and run a preview (no side effects) that reports diff-like outcomes
Dry-run mode executes runbook logic against a sandbox resource set and records recorded actions and simulated results
Every executed transaction emits an undo token that can be used to reverse the transaction within 72 hours or until manual revocation
Staged approval policy: high-risk transactions require a second approver; the UI/CLI surface shows approval status and audit trail
Structured telemetry (token-id, step-id, resource-ids, duration, success/failure) is available in Console and can be exported to BigQuery for post-mortem analysis
steps: Design API schema for Transaction, Step, PreviewResult, and UndoToken
Prototype in a feature branch: implement transaction coordinator and dry-run adapter
Wire Console UI: transaction builder, preview diff view, approval workflow
Integrate with runbook task executor and existing RBAC checks
Add telemetry hooks and logging to tracing pipeline
Write e2e tests and a simulated-sandbox harness for CI
decisions: Use the existing runbook-as-task API surface instead of duplicating DSL to minimize maintenance
Undo tokens will be opaque UUIDs tied to recorded compensation actions (no plan to expose raw reversal scripts by default)
Sandbox will be implemented initially as a namespaced staging resource layer with mock connectors for third-party services
Approval gating: leverage existing SSO groups and console approver UI rather than building a separate approval service
comments: 2026-02-24 — Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after product design workshop. Draft spec uploaded to Confluence. (see attachments).

2026-02-26 — Liam O'Connor: Spike completed — coordinator prototype that sequences steps and stores a reversible action log. Spike branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/admin-playground/pull/42
2026-03-02 — PM review (Noah Patel): Requested stronger guardrails for 'destructive' primitives and an explicit SLO for undo window. Action: add staged approvals and 72-hour undo expiry.

2026-03-05 — Security review (Rina Gomez): Completed high-level threat assessment; recommended deny-by-default for connectors that access external customer systems. Follow-up: add feature flag and audit-only mode for first release.
2026-03-08 — Design feedback (Aria Singh): Mockups refined to emphasize 'Preview' and 'Undo' affordances; added visual confirmation step for irreversible actions.

2026-03-10 — QA (Ethan Brooks): Began writing test matrix for dry-run vs execution scenarios; found edge case where step timeouts can leave partial resources — mitigation: include compensating step generator in coordinator.
2026-03-12 — Liam O'Connor: Implementation in progress; core transaction coordinator landed on feature branch. Next: integrate RBAC checks and wire telemetry events.
notes: Trade-offs: full transactional guarantees across heterogeneous external systems are infeasible; we implement an eventual-compensation model (recorded compensation steps generated at plan-time). This means some reversals are best-effort and documented in the audit trail. We prioritized safety and observability over atomicity for the initial ship.
next_steps: Merge coordinator basic flow behind feature flag (feature/admin-playground)
Implement compensating action generator and attach to transaction metadata
Add approval policy enforcement and UI hooks
Roll out internal dogfood to SRE and first-line support with audit-only mode
Collect telemetry for 2 weeks and iterate on false-positive/negative for undo effectiveness
